$comment: Gemfall beat 3 on the River Road (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 3A). Every ending sets exactly one member of `crossing`: rest_dry_end sets crossed_dry on entry; scene_swept sets river_took_us on entry and is the only door to rest_wet_end and rest_setback. The two never share a path - scene_swept is reached only from a missed crossing activity or failed crossing check or a lost drake fight, and rest_dry_end only from a completed crossing activity or passed crossing check. The setback needs a swept party to fail a crawler check AND lose the crawler fight. The expansion's episodes (kettle camp, wagon, river view, passes, Dilly, gem toll, camp vote, night rope, wake fee, east landing, mouth shore) set only chapter-local flags.
title: The Long Mile

plate.narration: At Stone Crossing, a mossy troll rests one enormous palm on the first stone. A bird is building a nest on his shoulder. The line can wait. Every traveler owes him a story or a riddle.

objectives.label: Put the centaurs' road markers back
Got a fair rate from the river drake

goal.text: Pay the toll at Stone Crossing and get across the river.

steps.label: Camp in the line for the night

facet_drakes_rate.name: The Drake's Rate
facet_drakes_rate.text: The newest piece on a river drake's hoard shelf. Marked PAID, underlined twice.

ossley_reed_knot.name: Ossley's Reed Knot
ossley_reed_knot.text: A reed knot from Old Ossley. "Later. When I'm going your way." It never dries.

scene_east_road.narration: Marda's rumor board said the crossing line was moving again. Tonight, pay the troll's toll at Stone Crossing and get across the Great River. First comes the Long Mile. Its markers are missing. Someone is cooking porridge on the stump marked MILE 3. It smells like a mistake.

choices.label: Read the clues and rebuild the marker line
Wave first, the old road way
Keep walking to the crossing
Set the posts by eye; risk losing the guide

check_markers.prompt: Put the mile markers back in the right order

onSuccess.narration: Mile one, mile two, mile three, all the way to the river. A centaur gallops up, counts them twice, and looks like she might cry with relief.

onFailure.narration: Every marker goes back in. MILE 7 goes back in between MILE 2 and MILE 3, so the road now runs backwards for a bit. A centaur thunders past, groans, and fixes it without stopping. No guide for you today.

scene_courtesy.narration: You wave first, from far off, tail curled politely away, the way road peoples have done for longer than anybody remembers. A centaur on the ridge stops dead, puts a hand on her heart, and waves back so hard her sash ribbons tangle.

choices.label: Go and say hello properly

scene_fennick.narration: Fennick Longstride, a road-warden centaur, checks her stitched map-sash. "At the crossing, use the upstream edge. The stones are only half under there." She points out the line, then trots ahead to check her detour signs.

choices.label: Walk on toward the river

scene_queue.narration: At Stone Crossing, giant flat stones cross the narrow river. The line fills the road. Someone sells line soup. Someone sells a map of the line. Near the front, six brass hats are quietly moving the line rope. "Don't mind us," one says, smiling.

choices.label: Call the brass hats out
Fly up and catch them at it
Let it go and wait your turn

check_rivals.prompt: Find the fresh brass-hat knots in the line rope

onSuccess.narration: You point out that the rope has fresh knots, the knots are brass-hat knots, and one of them still has a brass hat caught in it.

onFailure.narration: The Brassbuckles smile, tip their six matching hats, and are somehow forty places ahead of you. Nobody saw anything. Everybody saw everything.

scene_rivals_caught.narration: A troll sends the Brassbuckle Expedition and its six matching hats to the back. They leave a rope tied across the shallows: their secret shortcut, now available to you.

choices.label: Take your place in the line

scene_troll.narration: The toll-troll, Old Lintel, rests a mossy palm on the first stone. "A story," he rumbles. "Or a riddle." Every traveler owes one. Take a moment to tell yours aloud. A bird begins a nest on his shoulder. He has plenty of time.

choices.label: Tell him a story
Ask him a riddle
Make up a brand-new story, right now
Bring him the prides' riddle score

scene_troll_riddle_account.narration: You bring him the prides' riddle score, the way manticores have for generations. Old Lintel reads the total. His total is different. His total has always been different. He makes a sound like two boulders being pleased with each other, writes your names under both numbers, and presses a smooth luckstone into your palm "for keeping the argument going."

choices.label: Wait for the next toll

scene_troll_ask_riddle.narration: Ask your riddle aloud. Old Lintel tries answers like stones in a wall. Then he asks one so old that nobody knows its last word. He accepts your guess because you meant it.

choices.label: Wait for the next toll

scene_troll_tell_story.narration: Old Lintel hears every word of your story. The bird finishes its nest. At last he rumbles, "Good. That one's paid."

choices.label: Wait for the next toll

scene_troll_hum.narration: Old Lintel stops listening to the line and starts listening to the bridge. "The stones are humming," he rumbles. "Every pack in this line, and the whole road behind it. A note older than this bridge, and this bridge is not young." Stories and riddles are not enough this season. Now there is one more toll, and it is a question he asks everyone: "Where did you get that? And where is it going?"

choices.label: Answer him honestly
Admit you don't know yet
Show him the Ember Facet

scene_troll_hum_show_ember.narration: You hold out the Ember Facet. Old Lintel does not take it. He lays one finger near it on the stone of the bridge, and the bridge hums back, the same low note, so deep you feel it in your boots. "There," he says. "Hear that? Older than me." He looks at the stone for a long time, and then at you.

choices.label: Join the line camp

scene_troll_hum_dont_know.narration: "Don't know yet," you say. Old Lintel nods, which takes a while. "Then that's the toll," he says. "Find out." He has clearly decided that this counts as paying, and nobody argues with a troll about tolls.

choices.label: Join the line camp

scene_troll_hum_answer_honest.narration: You tell him about the red stone that landed by your boot at the Exchange, and where you think all of them are going, as honestly as you can. Old Lintel listens all the way to the end. "Good," he says. "Keep asking it. Of everyone." He lifts his palm off the stone just long enough to wave you toward the line camp.

choices.label: Join the line camp

rest_queue_camp.narration: The line camps for the night. Toffee is shared, then stolen by a goat. Rest and listen to the river. Under the bridge, something rubs numbers off a slate and writes larger ones.

choices.label: Look under the bridge
Settle down to sleep

scene_drake_shelf.narration: In the bridge's shadow, a river drake lies along a rock shelf like a cat on a windowsill. The shelf holds fish bones, three boat hinges, one otter-polished pebble, and right in the middle a new gem that hums. Beside it, a slate says RATES, and the drake keeps rubbing the numbers out with its tail and writing bigger ones.

choices.label: Offer the drake a fair trade
Offer it a honeycake, the way the ferrymen do
Grab the gem while it blinks
Leave it. Rates are rates.

check_drake.prompt: Haggle with a river drake who has done this before

onSuccess.narration: You offer a song, a shiny button, and a really excellent fish story. The drake weighs all three, decides it has been treated like a professional, and nudges the humming gem across the shelf.

onFailure.narration: The drake listens to your offer, then raises its rates. Then it raises them again, just to watch your face. The humming gem stays exactly where it is.

scene_drake_deal.narration: The new gem is warm, and it hums against your palm like a cat purring under a blanket. The drake writes PAID on its slate, underlines it twice, and goes back to timing the line.

choices.label: Back to camp for the night

encounter_drake.narration: The drake does not blink after all. Its sister surfaces beside it. She handles complaints.

onVictory.narration: Splashed, soaked, and outplayed, the two drakes huddle and mutter. "Fair," huffs the big one at last. "You won the rate."

onDefeat.narration: A tail as long as a canoe sweeps you, quite politely, off the shelf and into the current. Rates are rates.

scene_crossing_bank.narration: Your turn at last. Brown water hides the last stepping stones. Wait for a lull and cross, or use a line you prepared for a wider safe window. You can also risk a quick scramble. A frog in a flat boat watches from the reeds. His hat looks older than the line.

choices.label: Wait for a lull, then cross the drowned stones
Take Fennick's shallow line
Use the Brassbuckles' rope
Fly a rope across first
Step only where the heron stepped
Take the slow line you watched all evening
Ask the frog in the boat
Use the rope you saved in the night
Scramble straight across; risk the current

scene_ossley_price.narration: That is Old Ossley. He ferries when the stones are under, and he has never once asked for coin. He looks you over and asks for three small things: the song you hum when nobody is listening, the last thing you were proud of, and a promise to carry something for somebody, someday. He does not say what. He does not say who.

choices.label: Accept the promise and balance the ferry
Thank him and wade instead

check_crossing.prompt: Step from drowned stone to drowned stone across the last stretch

onSuccess.narration: Slip, wobble, step, step, step. The river grabs at your ankles, grumbles, and lets go. You stand on the east bank with boots that are, astonishingly, dry, in the middle of a traffic jam.

onFailure.narration: One stone is not where it was yesterday. The river decides it wants you more than the bank does, and everybody goes in together with a splash that startles a heron into next week.

check_crossing_easy.prompt: Hold on tight through the last fast stretch

onSuccess.narration: The current tugs, and sulks, and lets you go. Your boots touch the east bank and they are, astonishingly, dry.

onFailure.narration: Right at the fastest bit, a drake's wake rolls by, and the river decides it wants you more than the bank does. Everybody goes in together with a splash that startles a heron into next week.

rest_dry_end.narration: The east bank. The Eastern Plains roll away ahead, gold and green, and behind you a caravan is still telling the troll its story. On the far ridge a manticore silhouette waves first. Wave back. Camp here tonight, dry, with the river in your ears and that older note humming in your packs.

variants.text: Your road-marker work needed a centaur's help. Her checked line was part of your preparation.
The night rescue worked with the troll's help. The borrowed rope bore his muddy thumbprint.
The ferryman called your steps or steadied your load. You reached this bank with help.

scene_swept.narration: The river carries you south like a parcel nobody signed for. Past the line, past the Sunward banks, past a heron who watches the whole thing with deep disapproval. It goes on for a long, long time, and the heron follows, just to keep disapproving.

choices.label: Hold on tight
Float on your backs like starfish

scene_mouth.narration: At last the river lets you go, in the shallows near its mouth, on the eastern shore. Pale haze hangs over the Bone Yard far away. And sitting in a perfectly dry boat in the reeds, as if he had been waiting for you, is a frog in a very old hat. He fishes you out one at a time and says nothing. Then he says his name, "Ossley," just once, as if you had better remember it. Then: "Later. When I'm going your way." He presses a wet reed knot into your hand, and it stays wet.

choices.label: Squelch up the beach

scene_crawlers.narration: The beach is covered in old bone chips laid out in neat spirals. Then a spiral stands up. Bone crawlers: little scuttlers wearing shells of borrowed fossil, sleeves too long, dignity enormous. They are clattering straight for your humming packs.

choices.label: Throw something shiny the other way
Stand tall and leave loudly
Shoo them off

check_crawlers.prompt: Fool a bone crawler swarm with something that glitters

onSuccess.narration: You fling a wet, glinting spoon down the beach. Every crawler turns at once and pours after it like a rattling carpet. Somewhere behind you, you hear them start arranging it in a spiral.

onFailure.narration: The spoon glitters. Your packs hum. The crawlers are not stupid. They clatter around the spoon and keep coming.

check_crawlers_leave.prompt: Stomp off the beach looking as big as you possibly can

onSuccess.narration: Arms up, elbows out, stomping like giants. The crawlers decide you are far too large to bother with and scuttle back to their spirals, muttering.

onFailure.narration: Somebody stomps into a rock pool, sits down very suddenly, and is no longer the biggest thing on the beach. The crawlers notice.

encounter_crawlers.narration: The crawlers spread through the reeds in a clatter, all aiming for whatever hums.

onVictory.narration: Bopped, flipped, and outrun, the crawlers clatter off in a huff to rearrange their spirals and pretend this never happened.

onDefeat.narration: There are a lot more of them than there looked. The crawlers swarm over the packs like a rattling blanket.

rest_wet_end.narration: You build a driftwood fire on the eastern shore and steam gently, like dumplings. North of here the Eastern Plains are waiting, and you will walk into them from the south, the wet way, the way almost nobody does. Old Ossley's boat is gone. The knot in your pocket is still damp, and you suspect it always will be.

variants.text: Your road-marker work needed a centaur's help. Her checked line was part of your preparation.
The night rescue worked with the troll's help. The borrowed rope bore his muddy thumbprint.
The ferryman called your steps or steadied your load. You reached this bank with help.

rest_setback.narration: The crawlers carry off the snacks, two bootlaces and the map, none of which hum but all of which they apparently wanted. By the time you've chased your boots down, the whole day is gone. Old Ossley poles past without stopping and nods once, as if to say: you'll still get there. Just later.

scene_kettle_camp.narration: A camp is boiling its kettle on painted firewood. THIS WAY AROUND. NOT THAT WAY. GO UPSTREAM, PLEASE. Those are the centaurs' detour signs. The campers have mistaken a warning for a very colorful log.

choices.label: Swap them your kindling for the signs
Explain what the signs are for

scene_kettle_camp_swap_kindling.narration: You trade your whole bag of kindling for the signs. The campers think this is a wonderful deal, because kindling burns better than paint. You walk on with an armful of arrows that all point different ways, which makes you look extremely lost.

choices.label: Carry the signs on down the road

check_kettle.prompt: Tell the campers which sinkhole each painted sign steers wagons around, before the kettle whistles

onSuccess.narration: You explain that the signs steer wagons around the new sinkholes and away from the river's fast bits. The campers go pink, stand every sign back up by the road, and pour you tea to say sorry. It is excellent tea.

onFailure.narration: The campers nod, and nod, and say "oh, absolutely," and then set the kettle back down on NOT THAT WAY. You leave them arguing about which way that way is.

scene_stuck_wagon.narration: A wagon is axle-deep in a rut. Its driver folds his arms. "Admiring the view," he says. The view is mud. You can push hard, or unload the humming crates to take the weight off.

choices.label: Put your shoulders to the wheels
Help him unload the crates first
Have a thornguard brace the wheel for everyone

check_wagon.prompt: Everybody heave a loaded wagon out of a rut

onSuccess.narration: One, two, HEAVE! The wagon pops out of the rut like a cork from a bottle. The driver says he was just about to do that himself, and gives you a honeycake for your trouble anyway.

onFailure.narration: One, two, HEAVE! Nothing. Again! Nothing. The mule sighs, leans into its harness, and pulls the whole wagon out by itself, looking at you as if you were luggage.

scene_stuck_wagon_unload.narration: You lift down the humming crates. "Gems for the north," says the driver. The lighter wagon rolls out. "Still admiring the view," he adds, putting his hat back on.

choices.label: Wave him off and walk on

scene_river_view.narration: Stone Crossing stretches into brown water. A gray heron fishes from a half-drowned stone. Below the bridge, a river drake flicks its whiskered tail: a small river dragon with strong opinions about money. On the slope, a centaur searches empty posts for her signs.

choices.label: Follow the heron through the drowned stones
Buy a map of the line from a boy with a tray
Give the centaur her detour signs back
Glance from the ridge; risk missing its line

check_heron.prompt: Learn the crossing by watching a heron fish it

onSuccess.narration: Left foot, right foot, never the middle. The heron only ever steps on the upstream edge of the stones, where they are only half under. You learn its line by heart. The heron notices you learning it and looks deeply offended.

onFailure.narration: The heron catches you staring. It stares back. It is much better at staring than you are, and by the time you blink it has flown off with a fish, and you have learned nothing at all except humility.

scene_river_view_queue_map.narration: The map of the line costs one button. It is a long wiggly sausage with YOU ARE HERE written at the very end, which turns out to be completely correct. On the back, in pencil, somebody has copied out the river drake's rates from last week. They were a lot smaller last week.

choices.label: Join the end of the sausage

scene_river_view_give_signs.narration: It's Fennick Longstride, the road-warden centaur, and when she sees her signs she hugs them like lost puppies. She hammers each one back on its post, and on the last one she scratches a new arrow pointing at the upstream edge of the crossing, where the stones are only half under. "For you," she says, and gallops off.

choices.label: Follow her arrow down to the line

scene_skip_passes.narration: The six brass hats call themselves the Brassbuckle Expedition. One strolls down the line selling SKIP PASSES. "Skip the line!" he sings. The small print is tiny. Old Lintel takes stories at the front. He does not appear to be taking passes.

choices.label: Read the small print
Say it loud: stories are the toll

check_small_print.prompt: Read the tiny writing on a SKIP-A-STORY pass

onSuccess.narration: You squint. In letters the size of ants it says: VALID ON DAYS WHEN THE RIVER RUNS UPHILL. You read it out loud. The whole line laughs, and the Brassbuckle sells exactly no passes at all. She tips her hat to you, quite sportingly.

onFailure.narration: The print is so small it might just be ants. One of the letters walks away. You hand the pass back politely, and the Brassbuckle moves on down the line, selling briskly.

scene_skip_passes_no_thanks.narration: "Stories are the toll," you say. Nearby families put away their purses. The Brassbuckle turns her tray around. It now says COLLECTIBLE PASSES. Business does not improve.

choices.label: Shuffle forward in the line

scene_first_story.narration: A girl named Dilly is practicing her first troll story. "I have the start," she whispers, "but no ending." Help her invent one, or give her your own best story and make up a fresh one at the toll.

choices.label: Help her find an ending
Give her your best story to keep

scene_first_story_help_ending.narration: Everyone suggests an ending. Dragon? Wedding? Sandwich? Dilly picks the sandwich and practices it until she stops whispering. The troll is ready for her.

choices.label: Your turn at the toll

scene_first_story_give_story.narration: You give Dilly your best story, beginning to end. She runs off to practice. Now you need something new for Old Lintel. Behind you, Dilly gives your best line a magnificent roar.

choices.label: Your turn at the toll

scene_troll_new_story.narration: You make up a story on the spot. It wobbles. It has a goat in it for no reason. Old Lintel listens to every wobble, and at the end he says, "Never been told before. Rare, that." Out on the far stones, Dilly turns around and waves. Her story was a big hit.

choices.label: Wait for the next toll

scene_gem_toll.narration: A prospector slaps a humming gem on the bridge. "Paid!" Old Lintel does not move. The bridge hums the same note. Explain the story toll, or lift the gem and test whether the bridge's hum stops.

choices.label: Whisper that the toll here is a story
Lift the gem off the bridge

scene_gem_toll_explain.narration: "A story or a riddle," you whisper. The prospector goes red. "I wanted a gem. I got a gem. The end." Old Lintel considers this. The bird waits. "Paid," he says.

choices.label: Listen to what the troll does next

scene_gem_toll_lift_gem.narration: You lift the gem. The bridge stops humming. Set it down: the note returns. Old Lintel watches your hands, then rests his enormous palm beside the gem.

choices.label: Hand the prospector his gem

choice_camp_spot.narration: Choose one camp job before bed. The goat family offers a honeycake, useful for trading with the drake. Beside the brass hats, you can stop their rope scheme without a scramble. By the water, you can learn a wider, slower crossing window. You cannot sleep in all three places. The goat has tried.

choices.label: Next to the goat family
Next to the brass hats, to keep an eye on them
Down by the water, to learn the river

choice_camp_spot_by_goat.narration: The goat eats a map and most of a hat. Its family apologizes with a honeycake. Keep it for the drake if you want a trade. Keep it away from the goat either way.

choices.label: Unroll your blankets

choice_camp_spot_by_brass.narration: Beside the Brassbuckles, you hear whispers and a rope being coiled. They stop whenever you look up. If they sneak out tonight, you will be close enough to sit on their rope.

choices.label: Unroll your blankets

choice_camp_spot_by_water.narration: You watch the current: fast in the middle, slower at the upstream edge. By bedtime you know the longer lull to use tomorrow. Your socks have learned the river too.

choices.label: Unroll your blankets

scene_night_rope.narration: A midnight splash. The Brassbuckles are sneaking across with a rope. The black river tugs at its first traveler. Brace the line to earn its use tomorrow, wake the troll, or stop them from your nearby camp.

choices.label: Brace the rope together before pulling
Wake Old Lintel
You're right beside them. Sit on their rope.
Have a duskrunner slip down to the water ahead of them

check_night_rope.prompt: Everybody grab the Brassbuckles' rope before the river does

onSuccess.narration: You grab the rope just as the river grabs the first Brassbuckle. Everybody pulls. Out he pops, soaked, minus his hat, and says thank you so quietly you nearly miss it. All six creep back to their places in the line and stay there.

onFailure.narration: The rope zips through your hands, but the Brassbuckles grab it too, and everybody ends up in one dripping heap on the bank. One brass hat sails off downstream, spinning. Nobody says anything. Everybody goes back to bed.

scene_night_rope_wake_troll.narration: You shake Old Lintel's arm. You shake it again. Trolls wake up the way mountains do: slowly. By the time he has opened one eye, the Brassbuckles have looked at the black water, changed their minds, and crept back to bed. Old Lintel closes the eye. "Good," he rumbles, to nobody in particular.

choices.label: Back to your blankets

scene_night_rope_sit_on_rope.narration: You are sleeping right next to them, so you simply roll over and sit on the rope. The Brassbuckles tug. You sit. They tug harder. You yawn. In the end they give up and go back to bed, muttering, and you get the best sleep of the whole trip, on a very lumpy rope.

choices.label: Sleep till morning

scene_wake_fee.narration: Morning. A drake has put up WAKE FEE: ONE GOOD JOKE. An unpaid drake might race past your crossing for fun. You can risk a joke, offer a fish, or use a trade you earned.

choices.label: Tell the drake a joke
Pay it a fish from the line soup
Show it the stone it marked PAID
Have a songkeeper sing the drake its fee
Pay the drake a coin and skip the joke

onSuccess.narration: "What do you call a fish with no eyes? A fsh." A long silence. Then the water bubbles and bubbles: the drake is laughing so hard it has to come up for air. It taps the slate with its tail. PAID.

onFailure.narration: You tell your best joke. The drake looks at you. You explain the joke. The drake looks at you harder. Then it writes NOTED on the slate, which is somehow worse than not laughing, and sinks out of sight.

scene_wake_fee_pay_fish.narration: You fish a fish out of the line soup and hold it out, dripping. The drake takes it with enormous dignity, checks it against a chart only it can see, and writes PAID. The soup seller looks into her pot, counts, and decides not to ask.

choices.label: Step up to the water

scene_wake_fee_show_paid.narration: You hold up the Drake's Rate, with PAID underlined twice. The drake in the water squints at it, recognizes its own handwriting, and huffs with deep professional respect. It wipes the slate clean and writes, very neatly: FRIENDS AND FAMILY RATE.

choices.label: Step up to the water

scene_east_landing.narration: On the east bank, a donkey named Parsnip blocks the carts. Her driver says she refuses to stand near humming gem crates. Parsnip lies down with her eyes shut, to make her position clear.

choices.label: Move the humming crates to the last cart
Ask the driver Old Lintel's question

scene_east_landing_move_crates.narration: You move the humming crates to the last cart. Parsnip gets up and leads the line. "A lot of fuss," says the driver, secretly giving her an apple.

choices.label: Find a dry spot to camp

scene_east_landing_ask_question.narration: "Where did you get them? Where are they going?" The driver studies his crates. "Off the rush. North, to whoever pays." Parsnip snorts. Nobody has a better answer yet.

choices.label: Find a dry spot to camp

scene_swept_float.narration: Everybody lets go of being scared and floats on their back, arms and legs out, like a row of starfish. The river seems to like this better. It carries you more gently, around the bends and past the reeds, and the heron flies along overhead, disapproving of the starfish too.

choices.label: Drift where the river takes you

scene_mouth_shore.narration: You wring out your socks on the shore. Somebody's hat comes bobbing down the river, spins twice, and washes up at your feet. All along the tide line, little chips of old bone lie in spirals, hundreds of them, neat as a garden. The heron lands on a rock and looks at your wet socks with total disapproval.

choices.label: Look closely at the spirals
Do the drying-off dance

check_spirals.prompt: Trace each bone-chip spiral with a finger and find what it curls around

onSuccess.narration: The spirals are not random. Each one curls around a bare patch where something humming must have lain, and every chip leans away from it, like grass in a wind. Even the beach flinches from the stones. Your packs hum. Somewhere up the beach, something rattles.

onFailure.narration: You count spirals until you lose count, and start again, and lose count again. The heron watches you do it three times, cannot bear it, and flies off. Somewhere up the beach, something rattles.

scene_mouth_shore_dry_dance.narration: You do the drying-off dance: hop, shake, flap, hop. It is not a real dance, but it works, mostly. The heron does not join in. A little way up the beach the bone chips begin to rattle, as if something there liked the music.

choices.label: Go and see what's rattling

interaction_planks.narration: With the wagon free, you and the driver lay planks across its deep rut. The carts behind stop honking long enough to help. Someone puts a kettle on the last plank to make sure it stays. The last plank drops into the rut, flat and snug. The first cart behind rolls over it without a single bump, and the driver presses a few coins into your hand. "Plank money," he says gruffly. "I was admiring the view, but I am also grateful."

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_hats.narration: Another of the brass hats has set up a little game on an upturned barrel, hoping to win back what the passes did not earn. Three brass cups. One shiny button. "Watch the button!" she calls to the line. "Find it, and there's a prize from my tray. Miss it, and you only lose your dignity!" She slides the button under the middle cup, and her hands begin to fly.

interaction.cue: Watch the glow, then choose the cup with the button.

onSuccess.narration: You lift the right cup, and there is the button, winking at you. The line cheers. The Brassbuckle grumbles, tips her hat and pays up with a little brass whistle from her tray. "One tweet," she says, "and think of me kindly."

onFailure.narration: You lift the wrong cup. Under it there is nothing but a very small spider, who looks offended. The Brassbuckle bows to the line. "Better luck in the next line!" she sings, and the spider goes back to bed.

onAssisted.narration: The Brassbuckle slows her hands, grinning, until the whole line can follow the button. You lift the right cup, and she pays up with a little brass whistle from her tray. "One tweet," she says, "and think of me kindly."

interaction_hum.narration: Old Lintel hums his low note and lets you listen until it settles in your ears. The ground seems to hum beneath it. "Remember that," he says. "Songs travel farther than lines." You hum it back, low, high, middle, low, and under your boots the bridge hums with you, very faintly. Old Lintel's mossy face does something that might be a smile. "There," he says. "You will know it again." He puts his palm back on the stone and waves you toward the line camp.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_pot.narration: The cook calls you back to her enormous supper pot. Together you tip a fat brown ribbon of porridge into the waiting bowls. The line can wait while everyone gets something warm. She wraps a hot supper for you. "Better than the porridge at MILE 3," she says. "That is not hard." Down the road, a wagon is stuck across the way.

choices.label: Continue together

scene_crab_dusk.narration: Blankets down, supper started, the sky gone orange. Then the river goes click. Two crabs haul themselves up the bank, and their shells are clear as windowpanes, with a faint glow inside. Glassback crabs. Every pack in the line is humming, and the crabs have decided that the humming is a dinner bell. They are marching for the gem carts at the end of the line, claws high, and a row of sleepy mules is starting to wake up and complain. "Somebody do something!" cries the soup seller. "They'll tip the whole line!"

choices.label: Shoo the crabs back to the water

encounter_crabs.narration: The crabs click and clatter up the bank, claws high, all aiming for whatever hums. Turn them around before they reach the carts.

scene_crabs_turned.narration: The crabs rock from side to side, grumble, and back down the bank into the water, shells flashing, as if they had only come to look. The mules go back to sleep. The soup seller has watched the whole thing with her ladle raised like a sword. She lowers it and presses a warm bottle into your hands. "Waiting tonic," she says. "On the house. Do not tell the others."

choices.label: Back to your blankets

scene_crabs_sent_home.narration: The crabs keep coming, click, click, click, until far off at the front of the line Old Lintel simply lowers one enormous hand flat on the bridge. THUD. The whole bank shivers. The crabs freeze, take a long look at the hand, and scuttle back into the river, offended. Someone wraps blankets around you and hands out hot tea. There is no tonic tonight, but the mules are calm again.

choices.label: Back to your blankets

scene_wake_fee_pay_coin.narration: You drop a coin on the rock. The drake bites it, because it bites everything, rubs out WAKE FEE with its tail and writes PAID. Then, in smaller letters underneath, it adds PROMPT SERVICE. It sinks away looking extremely pleased with itself, and with you.

choices.label: Step up to the water

interaction_markers.narration: The numbers have washed off three posts. One shows a kettle, one a wagon rut, one the crossing. Match the travelers' clues to put them back from this end of the road. The kettle post smells of breakfast. That is not an official clue.

interaction.cue: Share the clues. Put the places in road order, nearest first.
clues: The kettle camp comes before the wagon rut.
The crossing comes after the wagon rut.
Start at this end of the road, not the river.

onSuccess.narration: Kettle, rut, crossing. A road-warden spots the straight line of posts and trots over to help you in return.

onFailure.narration: The crossing post goes before the kettle. A passing centaur corrects it, then gallops off to her other repairs. The road is marked, but she cannot stay to guide you.

onAssisted.narration: A passing centaur helps you compare the clues. Together you plant kettle, rut, crossing. She stays to show you her shallow crossing line.

interaction_heron.narration: The heron picks a half-drowned stone and steps between the reeds. Follow its glow through the moving reed clumps. You want its last fishing place, not a staring contest. The heron is undefeated at those.

interaction.cue: Follow the glow, then choose the heron's last position.

onSuccess.narration: You mark its last perch: the upstream edge. The heron leaves with a fish and the air of someone whose map has been copied.

onFailure.narration: You mark an empty patch of reeds. The heron has gone. At the crossing you can still ask the ferryman or try the ordinary stones.

onAssisted.narration: A traveler points out the glow as you follow. You mark the upstream edge together. It is a checked line, with help.

interaction_night_rope.narration: A brass hat bobs in the black water, followed by its owner. The rope is taut. Keep the bank end steady while the Brassbuckles climb out. Pulling harder is not the same as pulling together, although the wet man is suggesting both.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side until the rope marker is in the middle.

onSuccess.narration: The rope stays level. Out comes the soaked scout, then his hat. He lends you the bank rope for the morning crossing. It is the quietest thank-you of the trip.

onFailure.narration: The Brassbuckles get ashore in a dripping heap. Their rope washes away. Everyone is safe, but there is no spare line for morning.

onAssisted.narration: Old Lintel pins the rope with one enormous finger while you draw it in. Everyone gets ashore. The Brassbuckles lend you the rope for morning, with the troll's muddy thumbprint still on it.

interaction_crossing.narration: The brown current runs hard, then softens. Without a checked line, the lull is short. Watch the marker before stepping. The heron has appointed itself supervisor.

interaction.cue: Step when the marker is inside the gold lull.

onSuccess.narration: You step in the lull and reach the east bank dry. The heron finds nothing to complain about. It complains anyway.

onFailure.narration: You step into the hard current. Off the stones you go, heading for the southern shore.

onAssisted.narration: The ferryman calls the lull from his boat. With his help you step across and land dry.

interaction_crossing_prepared.narration: The brown current runs hard, then softens. Your prepared line marks the slower edge. You have longer to step. The heron has appointed itself supervisor.

interaction.cue: Step when the marker is inside the gold lull.

onSuccess.narration: You step in the lull and reach the east bank dry. The heron finds nothing to complain about. It complains anyway.

onFailure.narration: The wake catches your step. The river carries you off the stones toward the southern shore. Your prepared route cannot hold back the whole river.

onAssisted.narration: The ferryman calls the lull from his boat. With his help you step across and land dry.

interaction_ferry.narration: You offer your quiet song, a proud memory and a promise to carry something for someone someday. Old Ossley nods. Now keep the load level while he poles through the fast water. His hat does not wobble. It has had practice.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side to level the ferry load.

onSuccess.narration: The boat slips into the eastern reeds. Old Ossley gives one small nod. Dry boots, and a promise still to keep.

onFailure.narration: A wake tips the low boat. Old Ossley reaches for you as the current turns everyone south.

onAssisted.narration: Old Ossley shifts his pole to steady the load while you balance. The boat reaches the east bank dry.

voiceGuide.tone: warm, playful, a little spooky but never scary; a river crossing that is a real hazard and a busy, funny line

npcVoices.fennick: Fennick Longstride, a road-warden centaur; brisk, proud of her stitched route-sash, deeply offended that people burn road markers for firewood
npcVoices.old_lintel: a stone troll toll-taker, mostly moss; speaks very slowly, hears everything in full, palm always on the bridge; asks only 'where did you get that, and where is it going?'
npcVoices.drake: a river drake; semi-sapient, transactional, writes its rates on a slate; communicates in huffs, tail-taps and underlinings
npcVoices.brassbuckles: the Brassbuckle Expedition, six people in matching brass hats; smooth, smiling, always somehow ahead in the line
npcVoices.old_ossley: frogfolk ferryman; very few words, long pauses that are not hesitation; answers the question you meant; never asks for coin
npcVoices.kettle_campers: a rush camp boiling a kettle on the centaurs' detour signs; cheerful, agreeable, say 'oh, absolutely' and do not change
npcVoices.wagon_driver: a big rush wagon driver in a bigger coat, stuck in a rut, too proud to ask for help; 'admiring the view'
npcVoices.dilly: a small girl from a carpet caravan telling a troll her first ever story; nervous, then magnificent
npcVoices.prospector: a pushy prospector who tries to pay the troll toll with a gem; tells the shortest story ever told
npcVoices.parsnip_driver: a caravan driver landing on the east bank, arguing with his donkey Parsnip, secretly very fond of her

interaction_pot.narration: You have barely gone three steps when behind you something goes HISSSS. The camp's supper pot, a copper pot as big as a barrel, is boiling over, and the cook is waving her ladle like a flag. "Tip it off the fire before it scorches!" she cries. "One to tip, and everybody else to hold the pole!" There is porridge in there for the whole camp.

interaction.cue: Friends hold the pole steady while someone tips the pot.

onSuccess.narration: The pot tips slow and steady, and the porridge pours out in one fat brown ribbon into a row of waiting bowls. Not a drop in the fire. The cook mops her forehead with her sleeve and wraps a hot supper in a cloth for you. "Better than the porridge at MILE 3," she says. "That is not hard." Down the road, a wagon is stuck right across the way.

onFailure.narration: The pole wobbles, and the pot tips too soon. Porridge slides down the side in one slow slop and lands in the fire. Hiss. The cook looks at it for a while. "Crunchy," she says bravely. "We call it crunchy." Down the road, a wagon is stuck right across the way.

onAssisted.narration: The cook grabs the pole herself, and together you tip the pot slow and steady. The porridge pours out in one fat brown ribbon into a row of waiting bowls, and she wraps a hot supper in a cloth for you. "Better than the porridge at MILE 3," she says. "That is not hard." Down the road, a wagon is stuck right across the way.

interaction_planks.narration: The wagon is out, but the rut it leaves is deep as a bathtub, and a line of carts is already creeping up behind. "Planks!" cries the driver, pointing at a stack by the ditch. "Fill the rut before the next fellow sinks! Hand them down, hand them down!" So everyone lines up along the road, and the planks start to travel from hand to hand like a very slow train.

interaction.cue: Catch the plank, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: The last plank drops into the rut, flat and snug. The first cart behind rolls over it without a single bump, and the driver presses a few coins into your hand. "Plank money," he says gruffly. "I was admiring the view, but I am also grateful."

onFailure.narration: One plank goes in sideways and sticks up like a drawbridge. The first cart behind goes over it with a bump and a bang. The driver sighs, stamps it flat and says it will do. "It's a rut," he says. "It has had worse."

onAssisted.narration: The driver takes the middle of the line himself, and the planks fly down it, hand to hand to hand. The rut fills flat and snug, and he presses a few coins into your hand. "Plank money," he says gruffly. "I was admiring the view, but I am also grateful."

interaction_hum.narration: Before you step away, Old Lintel rumbles one more thing. "Hear the note first," he says. "Then you will know it when it comes around again." He hums it, low enough to rattle the pebbles: low, high, middle, low. "Now you," he says. "Hum it back."

interaction.cue: Listen to the note, then hum it back in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: You hum it back, low, high, middle, low, and under your boots the bridge hums with you, very faintly. Old Lintel's mossy face does something that might be a smile. "There," he says. "You will know it again." He puts his palm back on the stone and waves you toward the queue camp.

onFailure.narration: You hum a pretty tune. It is not the note. The bridge hums back, low and flat, as if politely correcting you. Old Lintel hums it once more, slower, and you get close enough. "Close," he says. "Close counts, for a first time." He puts his palm back on the stone and waves you toward the queue camp.

onAssisted.narration: Old Lintel hums along underneath you to hold the note up, low, high, middle, low, and the bridge hums with you, very faintly. "There," he says. "You will know it again." He puts his palm back on the stone and waves you toward the queue camp.
